title: Olmec Civilization
capsule: The Olmec civilization was the earliest major Mesoamerican culture, flourishing from roughly 1200 to 400 BCE in the tropical lowlands of present-day Veracruz and Tabasco, Mexico. San Lorenzo was the dominant center c. 1200–900 BCE, succeeded by La Venta c. 900–400 BCE; both sites feature colossal basalt portrait heads, monumental earthworks, and sophisticated jade carving indicative of complex chiefdom organization. The Olmecs established trade networks reaching throughout Mesoamerica and appear to have developed early forms of writing and the Mesoamerican calendar, making them foundational for the later Maya, Zapotec, and other civilizations.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Archaeological sites are well identified, but territorial extent is inferential based on artifact distribution since the Olmecs left no textual boundaries; their political organization remains debated.
